decisive_items: Evidence of ventricular interdependence and septal bounce
response.rationale: Constrictive pericarditis is supported by thickened pericardium, septal bounce/ventricular interdependence, and biventricular diastolic pressure elevation with exercise; restrictive cardiomyopathy is the closest mimic but lacks these pericardial and septal findings.

rejected.why: No pericardial effusion or tamponade physiology; thickened pericardium and constrictive hemodynamics favor constriction.
ECG changes alone are insufficient; negative viral studies and constrictive imaging/hemodynamics point to constriction rather than active myopericarditis.
Temporal association with vaccination is not diagnostic; preserved LVEF and constrictive findings favor constrictive pericarditis.
Nonspecific; no cardiomyopathy phenotype and thickened pericardium with septal bounce indicate constriction.
Overly broad; constrictive pericarditis is the specific subtype supported by imaging and hemodynamics.
Heart failure is a syndrome, not the underlying diagnosis; constrictive pericarditis is the cause.
Acute pericarditis would not explain thickened pericardium with constrictive physiology; ECG changes can accompany constriction.
